question: The Republic of Cyprus’ hydrocarbon reserves are very promising and can help the EU become energy independent. As is known, Türkiye is calling into question the Cypriot EEZ and at the same time is seeking to control the energy corridors of Central Asia with the aim of gaining greater bargaining power against the EU.

I stress the word ‘against’ because Ankara has, on a number of occasions, adopted a forceful and threatening stance when negotiating its path towards accession. Ankara's attempts to become an energy corridor via Asian countries and a transportation corridor for natural gas from the Cypriot EEZ via the occupied territories in Cyprus are of strategic importance. In view of this: 1.
Can the Commission say what steps it is taking to safeguard the EEZ of an EU Member State?
Is it considering ways of ensuring that the EU does not find itself in a tight spot in the event that Türkiye manages to strengthen its position and take a lead role in energy distribution?
answer: The framework governing the delimitation of the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of Member States is outlined in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which is generally considered to codify rules of customary international law. The EU is a party to this Convention.

Delimitation of the continental shelf and EEZ needs to be addressed through dialogue and negotiations in good faith, in accordance with international law, including the above United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The EU-Türkiye High Level Dialogue on Energy was suspended at political level in 2019 following the illegal drilling activities in the Eastern Mediterranean.

In the Joint Communication of 29 November 2023 (1), the Commission and the High Representative recommended — among other things — that the EU-Türkiye High-level Dialogue on Energy, be reinstated under the condition that Türkiye continues to refrain from all illegal drilling activities in the Eastern Mediterranean and all other actions that do not respect the sovereignty and sovereign rights of EU Member States.

At its meeting of 14-15 December 2023, the European Council took note of the report and agreed to revert on the matter at an upcoming meeting. While acknowledging the fact that Türkiye is a key partner in several areas and a candidate country for accession to the EU, the Commission follows closely the matter and will safeguard the rights of all Member States within the limits of its competences.
In line with the 2022 RePowerEU Plan, the EU is determined to diversify its energy supplies and suppliers.
